content:
The image shows a corn ear with:
- Dark brown/black discoloration at the tip of the ear
- Green/teal mold growth visible on the middle portion of the kernels
- Husks are pulled back, yellowed/dried
- Otherwise normal yellow kernels on the lower portion

The green mold coloration is the key feature here. Trichoderma ear rot is characterized by green mold growth on ears, caused by Trichoderma species which produce distinctive green conidia. The dark tip discoloration combined with the green/teal fungal growth on the kernels is classic for Trichoderma ear rot.

Gibberella ear rot typically shows pink/red mold starting from the tip. Diplodia shows white mold. Aspergillus shows yellow-green powdery mold. The green color here is more consistent with Trichoderma.
